2018_124_082118regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of August 21, 2018 at the Administration Building — the back-to-school meeting. It hires roughly sixty new teachers on probationary contracts, opens 85 ninth-grade Schools of Choice seats at International Academy East for 2019-2020, and authorizes an addendum to the D.M. Burr custodial contract raising the custodial minimum wage to $12.00 per hour at a base contract increase not to exceed $364,000. The June 2018 Treasurer's Report carries the year-end spike — $20,106,029.37 of total disbursements — and a bond and sinking fund update lays out a four-year Building Site and Sinking Fund plan against $3,900,000 of projected annual revenue.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, August 21, 2018, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the July 17, 2018 meeting, the June 2018 Treasurer's Report, and the IA-East Schools of Choice resolution.

**What the July 17 minutes record**
A short meeting (7:05 to 8:00 p.m.) that did a great deal of contractual work, all 7-0 unless noted. Two-year probationary administrative contracts to Christine Foren as Supervisor, Special Education and Jessica Carrier as Director, Special Education, both effective July 1, 2018. **The Superintendent's contract extended July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2021.** The four assistant and deputy superintendents — Mark Dziatczak, Rick West, Kris Griffor and Jordan Harris — extended through June 30, 2020. Twenty-nine other administrators' contracts extended through June 30, 2020; **Mr. Gottlieb excused himself from voting on this item for reasons of a personal nature** — the list includes Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity & Accountability — so it carried 6-0 with one abstention.

Troy High also joined Athens, Avondale and Berkley in a cooperative boys' and girls' skiing team for 2018-19 and 2019-20. And the Board certified ballot language for a **replacement operating millage** — restoring and replacing the authority to levy 18 mills on non-homestead property, approved by voters in 2015 and since rolled back by the Headlee Amendment, with headroom against future rollbacks — for the November 6, 2018 general school election, the wording due to the Oakland County Clerk no later than August 14, 2018.

**Treasurer's Report — June 2018**
June is the fiscal year's closing month and the numbers show it. Total check disbursements are **$17,527,051.55**, of which the General Fund group is $12,632,198.69 and the General Fund (101) itself $11,582,952.38. Adding $2,373,385.53 of wire transfers, $209,641.78 of P-Card purchases and $31,230.57 of ACH debits, less $35,280.06 of prior period voids, total disbursements in period are **$20,106,029.37**. Two lines show the capital program running at full speed: Building & Site Funds $3,271,337.13 and the Early Childhood Center Fund $724,608.21.

**Curriculum — 85 seats at IA East**
The Board adopts a Section 105c resolution accepting applications for **85 non-resident 9th grade students** who reside outside Oakland County, where that ISD is contiguous with Oakland ISD's boundaries, for the purpose of attending the International Academy East program located in the Troy School District. Unlike the elementary and middle school Schools of Choice resolutions adopted each February, this one is 105c only — IA East draws from beyond the county by design.

**Personnel — the August hiring class**
Probationary contracts for roughly sixty teachers for 2018-2019, heavily weighted toward the elementary grades and to special services. Hamilton alone takes six (Takouhy Kinzer and David Anderson in 3rd grade, Shalyn Fortuna in 1st, Ewa Dabrowski in 2nd, Christina Connolly in the resource room, Gabriella Mancini in the kindergarten resource room, plus Rebecca McNally in 3rd); Wattles takes five; Bemis four. The list includes six speech and language pathologists, three school social workers, a school psychologist, four resource room teachers and several early childhood program teachers at the Niles Center.

**Business — the custodial contract**
The Board authorizes administration to finalize an addendum to the Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services Contract with D.M. Burr Facilities Management, Inc. "to reflect the increased wages necessary to compete in the current labor market" — raising the aggregate contract price to reflect a **minimum wage of $12.00 per hour for custodians**, with the base contract increase not to exceed **$364,000** from the General Fund.

**Other — bond and sinking fund update**
Completed 2017 projects include Athens mechanical upgrades phase 2, mechanical and electrical upgrades at Barnard, Bemis and Wass, Administration Building mechanical upgrades, Athens and Troy High door replacements, the IA East kitchen renovation on MDE funds, the Troy High chiller replacement and roof replacements at six buildings. In process for 2018: mechanical and electrical upgrades at Costello, Leonard, Morse and Martell; hydronic piping replacements at Barnard, Bemis and Wass; an Athens vestibule for a special education entrance; an ADA-accessible ramp for the Troy Union stage; Bemis offices converted to a classroom; the Boulan old office renovation; and roofs at six more buildings.

The four-year Building Site and Sinking Fund projection is where the constraint shows. Against **$3,900,000 of projected revenue each year**, planned spending is $1,365,000 in 2018, **$6,160,000 in 2019**, $3,470,000 in 2020 and $3,345,000 in 2021 — the 2019 spike funded by carrying $2,535,000 forward from 2018 and drawing the balance down to $275,000, recovering to $705,000 and $1,260,000 thereafter. The 2019 bulge is mostly three items in the TSD approved projects line: **IAE at $2,000,000**, the Troy High pool at $250,000 and high school woods and autos at $250,000, plus a $150,000 board office.

A tennis court decision is put to the Board for Larson, Smith and International Academy/Baker: remove and replace four regulation courts at $55-$60K per court, $220-$240k per site, **$660-$720K total**, expected to last 7-8 years before requiring maintenance — or remove and restore with seed rather than sod at $30-$35K per site, **$90-$105K total**.

**Consent minutes: the July 17, 2018 regular meeting.** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart were present, along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators Dziatczak, Pagel, Young, Carrier and West, and two members of the audience. There were no recognitions and no additions or deletions. President Schmidt moved public communication for non-agenda items up on the agenda since one community member had asked to address the Board: Kristina Gerami, a Leonard parent, spoke regarding her concerns about specific information in her son's school records.

Resolution 18-062 approved the consent agenda 7-0: minutes of the June 5, 2018 meeting, the June 12, 2018 special meeting and closed session, the June 12, 2018 workshop and the June 19, 2018 meeting, plus the Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution for 2018/2019.

Resolution 18-063 issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Christine Foren as Supervisor, Special Education, effective July 1, 2018, carried 7-0. Resolution 18-064 issued the same form of contract to Ms. Jessica Carrier as Director, Special Education, effective July 1, 2018, carried 7-0.

Resolution 18-065 extended the contract of the Superintendent of Schools, in effect from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2021, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the provisions of the written agreement, carried 7-0.

Resolution 18-066 approved the extension of the contracts of Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, through June 30, 2020, without tenure in the administrative positions, carried 7-0.

Resolution 18-067 extended the contracts of the remaining administrators through June 30, 2020, or as otherwise indicated in the administrator's individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook where applicable and as permitted by law. Mr. Gottlieb excused himself from voting on this agenda item due to reasons of a personal nature, and the resolution carried 6-0 with Gottlieb abstaining — the list of administrators includes Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity & Accountability.

The administrators extended are: Ryan Brinks, associate principal, International Academy-East; Lara Dixon, principal, Athens High School; Remo Roncone, principal, Troy High School; Joe Duda, principal, Larson Middle School; Joyce Brasington, principal, Wattles Elementary; Brian Canfield, principal, Schroeder Elementary; Mike Cottone, principal, Troy Union Elementary; Erin Detmer, principal, Leonard Elementary; Tammy DiPonio, principal, Costello Elementary; Sarah Glasser, principal, Hamilton Elementary; Matt Jansen, principal, Wass Elementary; Melanie Morey, principal, Barnard Elementary; Jeremey Whan, principal, Bemis Elementary; Stephanie Zendler, principal, Morse Elementary; Melissa Curth, assistant principal, Troy High School; Robert Dowd, assistant principal, Athens High School; Dan House, assistant principal, Troy High School; Dan Mills, assistant principal, Athens High School; William Turner, assistant principal, Athens High School; Brian Zawislak, assistant principal, Troy High School; Amy Buchanan, assistant principal, Smith Middle School; David Recker, assistant principal, Larson Middle School; Kerry Birmingham, Director, Communications & Strategic Initiatives; Rob Carson, Director, Maintenance and Operations; Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity & Accountability; Christin Silagy, Director of ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments; and Elizabeth Soggs, Director, Technology.

Resolution 18-068 provided that Troy High School agrees to join Athens High School, Avondale High School and Berkley High School together to fund, support and maintain a cooperative team in the sport of boys' and girls' skiing for the 2018-19 and 2019-20 school years, carried 7-0.

Resolution 18-069 certified the ballot language for an operating millage proposal. It recites that the Board has determined it is necessary for the continuing operation of the School District to restore and replace the authority to levy 18 mills for operating purposes on non-homestead property, which was previously approved by the voters in 2015 and has been rolled back by application of the Headlee Amendment to the Michigan Constitution, and to increase the prior authority in the event of future rollbacks, as described in the Replacement Operating Millage Proposal attached as Exhibit A; that it is necessary and desirable to submit the proposal to the district's electors at the general school election to be held on November 6, 2018; and that in order to do so the Board must certify the ballot wording to the Clerk of the County of Oakland, the School District Election Coordinator, as required by Act 116, Public Acts of Michigan, 1954, as amended, not later than August 14, 2018. The resolution carried 7-0.

In board comments, Mrs. Hammond said she had reviewed the contracts and asked for more information, and Dr. Machesky said he and Rick West would be happy to meet with her to discuss further. Mrs. Fleming reported that the TFEE Golf Outing went very well and thanked Rick West and Rob Carson for their efforts in getting sponsors. Mr. Schmidt mentioned the next book study on "Growth Mindset" and suggested scheduling it for discussion sometime in November, brought up the D.M. Burr contract, and announced the next regular meeting on August 21 at 7:00 p.m. at the Administration Building along with a special workshop. The meeting adjourned at 8:00 p.m.

A fourth building and site fund, 418, appears in that line for the first time.

Total General Fund check disbursements are $12,632,198.69, and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS $17,527,051.55. Adding ACH debits of $31,230.57, outgoing wire transfers of $2,373,385.53 and P-Card purchases of $209,641.78, and subtracting prior period void disbursements of $35,280.06, TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD is $20,106,029.37 — by a wide margin the largest month in the fiscal year, as June closes out contracts, capital projects and the year's payroll obligations. The Early Childhood Center Fund, which first appeared at $3,715.00 in the February report, is now spending $724,608.21 a month, and the Building & Site funds $3,271,337.13.

**Consent item 5.C: Schools of Choice, Section 105c, 9th grade for 2019-2020.** In accordance with Michigan state law, school districts shall pass a resolution each school year if they intend to participate in a Schools of Choice program. It is anticipated that seats will be available for the 2019-2020 school year for grade 9 at the International Academy East, and the item proposes a Section 105c resolution for 85 non-resident 9th grade students who reside outside of Oakland County, if that intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries.

The resolution accordingly provides that the Board of Education of the Troy School District, exercising the option permitted by Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, will accept applications for a Schools of Choice program for the 2019-2020 school year for 85 non-resident 9th grade students who reside outside Oakland County, if that Intermediate School District is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, for the purposes of attending the International Academy East program located in the Troy School District. Unlike the paired 105/105c resolutions the Board adopts each February for elementary and middle school seats, this one is 105c only and an order of magnitude larger — 85 seats against the 40 kindergarten, 3 first grade and 14 middle school seats set six months earlier — because the International Academy is a consortium program drawing from beyond the county by design. It is also adopted more than a year ahead of the school year it governs.

The composition tells its own story about where the district was growing. The great majority are elementary positions, with 3rd grade the single most common assignment; Hamilton, Wattles, Bemis and Schroeder absorb the largest shares, matching the buildings named in the attendance area review as overcrowded. Special services are heavily represented — six speech and language pathologists, three school social workers, a school psychologist, four resource room teachers and several special education teachers — and three early childhood program teachers go to the Niles Center as the preschool program scales toward its new building.

**Business 8.A: the D.M. Burr contract addendum.** The item presents a resolution regarding negotiating an addendum to the Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services Contract with D.M. Burr Facilities Management, Inc. "to reflect the increased wages necessary to compete in the current labor market." The resolution authorizes administration to proceed with finalizing an addendum which will increase the aggregate contract price to reflect a minimum wage of $12.00 per hour for custodians, with the base contract increase not to exceed $364,000, approved as an expenditure of the General Fund. Mr. Schmidt had raised the D.M. Burr contract in board comments at the July 17 meeting, so the item arrives with the Board already briefed.

**Other 10.A: bond and Building Site and Sinking Fund projects update, August 2018.**

Completed 2017 projects: BP #8, Athens High School mechanical upgrades phase 2; BP #18, Barnard, Bemis and Wass mechanical upgrades (unit ventilators and HVAC units) and electrical upgrades (panels and fire alarm systems); Administration Building mechanical upgrades; Athens and Troy High School door replacements; the International Academy East kitchen renovation funded with MDE funds; BP #22, the Troy High School chiller replacement; and roof replacements at Barnard, Morse, Wattles, Athens, Troy High and IAE.

2018 projects in process: BP #21, Costello, Leonard, Morse and Martell mechanical upgrades (unit ventilators and HVAC units) and electrical upgrades (panels and fire alarm systems); Barnard, Bemis and Wass hydronic piping replacements; the Athens vestibule creation for a special education entrance; the Troy Union stage renovation adding an ADA-accessible ramp; the Bemis offices-to-classroom renovation; BP #24, the Boulan old office renovation; and roof replacements at Morse, Troy Union, Athens, Troy High, Niles and Transportation. Photo slides cover boiler replacements, unit ventilator replacements and controls upgrades, fire alarm systems, lighting and electrical upgrades, and door, window and roller shade replacements at Costello, Leonard, Morse and Martell; the Boulan old office and Bemis classroom renovations; the Troy Union stage; the Barnard, Bemis and Wass piping replacement; the six roof replacements; district-wide concrete replacement as needed; and BSSF flooring replacements at Athens, Boulan Park, Larson, International Academy, Bemis, Martell, Wass and Transportation.

2019 future bond projects: BP #23 covering Smith, Schroeder and Troy Union — electrical upgrades including fire alarm systems, HVAC and mechanical upgrades, door and window replacements, and boiler replacements at Schroeder and Troy Union — plus the Boulan Park and Larson locker replacement project; roofing at Troy High, Troy Union, Hill, Athens and IAE; and a Smith Middle School kitchen renovation from food service funds. 2019 future BSSF projects: Troy High auto and woodshop renovations; International Academy East remodeling including a pool area conversion and GROW office addition; Troy High pool remodeling; the IAE Boyd entrance paving project; the Hamilton parent drop-off drive project; gym floor refinishing at Larson and Boulan Park; playground and site upgrades at Barnard, Hill and Wass; district-wide concrete replacement by priority; district-wide asphalt patch and parking lot striping; district-wide fencing replacement by priority; district-wide flooring replacement per the five-year plan; district-wide casework replacement per the five-year plan; district-wide doors, windows and partitions replacement by priority and opportunity; and tennis court removal or replacement.

The four-year BSSF projection sets planned spending against a flat revenue line. Site improvements: paving at the IAE south entrance $75,000 in 2018, Hamilton $175,000 in 2019, IAE $600,000 in 2020 and Hill $250,000 in 2021, with district-wide paving repairs of $15,000 in 2018 and $250,000 in each following year; district-wide elementary hard play at $50,000 in 2019 and $100,000 in 2020 and 2021; district-wide fencing $75,000 then $100,000 annually; district-wide concrete $250,000 in 2018 and $150,000 thereafter; and playground improvements at Barnard, Hill and Wass ($250,000 in 2019), Martell, Morse and Schroeder ($250,000 in 2020) and Costello, Leonard and Troy Union ($250,000 in 2021) — totalling $415,000, $975,000, $1,450,000 and $1,100,000 across the four years.

Flooring and refinishing: the district-wide bid at $650,000 plus $50,000 of asbestos in 2018; in 2019 Morse $230,000, Schroeder $260,000, Troy Union $275,000, Smith $460,000, the Wattles café $60,000 and gym refinishing $100,000; in 2020 Wattles $185,000, Hill $260,000, Leonard $185,000, Larson and Boulan band rooms $40,000, an Athens allowance of $250,000 and $50,000 of gym refinishing; and in 2021 Barnard $250,000, Bemis $225,000, Martell $245,000, Costello $225,000, a district-wide allowance of $200,000 and $50,000 of gym refinishing — totalling $700,000, $1,385,000, $970,000 and $1,195,000. Windows and doors carry a district-wide budget of $100,000 in 2019 and $150,000 in each of 2020 and 2021; casework $200,000 annually from 2019; roofing $250,000 annually from 2019; and mechanical and electrical $250,000 for Smith unit ventilators plus $150,000 for Smith lights in 2019, then $250,000 annually.

TSD approved projects are the swing item: $15,000 for data processing, $30,000 for the Niles roof and ductwork and $5,000 for Athens MC in 2018, totalling $50,000; then in 2019 the Troy High pool at $250,000, high school woods and autos at $250,000, IAE at $2,000,000 and the board office at $150,000, totalling $2,650,000; and nothing in 2020 or 2021.

The totals are $1,165,000 in 2018, $5,960,000 in 2019, $3,270,000 in 2020 and $3,145,000 in 2021, plus $200,000 of soft costs each year, for $1,365,000, $6,160,000, $3,470,000 and $3,345,000. Projected revenue is $3,900,000 in each of the four years. Carry-over runs from nil in 2018 to $2,535,000 available in 2019, $275,000 in 2020 and $705,000 in 2021, with the closing balances $2,535,000, $275,000, $705,000 and $1,260,000. In other words, the fund underspends in 2018 to bank the money for a 2019 program that runs well over a single year's revenue, and the IAE line alone consumes more than half of that year's excess.

A final decision is put to the Board on tennis courts at Larson Middle School, Smith Middle School and International Academy/Baker. Remove and replace four regulation courts would cost $55-$60K per court, or $220-$240k per site, for a $660-$720K total, with an expectation of 7-8 years before the courts require maintenance. Remove and restore, seeding rather than sodding, would cost $30-$35K per site, or $90-$105K total. The presentation ends there, on a question rather than a recommendation.

Read as a whole, the August 2018 packet is the district's start-of-year meeting: roughly sixty new teachers hired at once, 85 out-of-county seats opened at IA East for the following year, a labor-market wage increase pushed through the custodial contract at up to $364,000, and a capital plan that has banked $2,535,000 to spend a year's revenue and a half in 2019. Behind all of it sits the millage the Board had put on the November 6 ballot the month before — a replacement of the same 18 non-homestead mills the district had been levying since 2015, eroded by Headlee.
